content.title: About
content.content: Dried pineapple consists of thin slices of fresh pineapple that have been dehydrated. It retains the fruit’s bright sweet‑tart flavor, aroma, and most of its nutrients, while offering a much longer shelf life.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dried pineapple is a common component of tropical trail mixes and granola.
The dehydration process removes up to 80 % of water, making the product lightweight and easy to transport.
Pineapple contains bromelain, an enzyme that helps break down proteins.
Some varieties are lightly sweetened or salted to enhance taste.
In many cultures dried pineapple is used in desserts, baked goods, and cocktails.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Dried pineapple retains a good amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains bromelain
items.content: Bromelain aids digestion, may reduce inflammation, and supports joint health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, helps you feel full, and assists in blood‑sugar regulation.

items.title: Provides magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals are important for heart, muscle, and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other dried fruits, dried pineapple is low in fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some dried pineapple products are sweetened, which can raise the glycemic index.

items.title: Pineapple allergy
items.content: People allergic to pineapple may experience skin rashes, swelling, or other reactions.

items.title: Sulfite additives
items.content: Sulfites are sometimes used to preserve color and may cause reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Dental risk
items.content: Sticky dried fruit can adhere to teeth and increase the risk of cavities if oral hygiene is inadequate.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried pineapple can be enjoyed as a snack, added to oatmeal, yogurt, baked goods, salads, or used in cocktails. Soaking it in water or juice briefly can restore some softness if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried pineapple in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For extended storage keep it in the refrigerator. Discard any pieces that become sticky, develop off‑odors, or show mold.
